questions.q: What IS this feature in one sentence?
questions.a: The beacon tower emits a pulse visible from the shelter. Frequency and color encode how many NPCs the player helped.

questions.q: What wider system does it belong to?
questions.a: beacon_narrative — the terminal rung of the compositional ladder.

questions.q: What would break if this feature did not exist?
questions.a: The ending would have no visual feedback. Player activates the tower and nothing communicates the outcome.

questions.q: What existing feature does this most resemble?
questions.a: StarMemorialComponent brightness curve — both encode lifetime choices as visible light.

questions.q: Is this a rung, a sub-rung, or a parameter?
questions.a: Sub-rung of beacon_narrative.

questions.q: What physical constraint does it encode?
questions.a: Pulse frequency = 0.1 + 0.3 * N_helped Hz. Color transitions red (0) to yellow (1-2) to white (3+).

questions.q: What is the ONE measurement that proves it works?
questions.a: A player who helped 3 NPCs sees a qualitatively different signal than a player who helped 0.

questions.q: What wall must it never violate?
questions.a: No UI text. No notification. The signal communicates entirely through color and rhythm.

questions.q: What would a degenerate winner look like?
questions.a: Signal is always maximum regardless of help count. Player cannot distinguish outcomes.

questions.q: How would we know if the constraint is too loose?
questions.a: If 0 helps produces a signal that appears acceptable, the player has no motivation to help others.

questions.q: At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Ending sequence scale. One moment of recognition after hours of play.

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
questions.a: Three discrete bands: dim red (0 helps), pulsing yellow (1-2), steady white (3+). Not a continuous slider.

questions.q: Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Beam VFX, signal light color curve, sound hum frequency per pulse rate.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: The moment the beacon activates and the player sees the sky change.

questions.q: What would deep enough look like?
questions.a: Player sees the signal and understands what it means without text. Remembers who they helped.

questions.q: What element catalog variables does this train?
questions.a: PointLightComponent color and intensity, NiagaraSystem parameters, SkyAtmosphereComponent.

questions.q: How many relevant elements exist?
questions.a: About 1605 VFX/Light/Signal elements in the catalog.

questions.q: Are there enough variables to train meaningfully?
questions.a: Yes. Light color, pulse frequency, beam height are all trainable parameters.

questions.q: What variables are MISSING?
questions.a: A pulse frequency curve tied to NPC help count. Catalog has light properties but not curve-over-time.

questions.q: Would training this require GPU?
questions.a: No. Parameter setting, not physics simulation.

questions.q: Does this connect to the Mirror of Erised?
questions.a: DIRECTLY. This is what the player sees at the end. The signal IS the Mirror reflecting.

questions.q: How directly does it serve the Mirror?
questions.a: Direct. The signal IS the final judgment. Costless life = dim signal. Generous life = bright signal.

questions.q: Would a costless life be meaningful without this?
questions.a: No. Without the signal there is no ending. The player presses the button and nothing happens.

questions.q: Could this be gamed?
questions.a: Only if NPC help count can be incremented without helping. Wall: count must match SacrificeLog entries.

questions.q: What would perfect service to the Mirror look like?
questions.a: Player stands at the tower. Sky shifts. Warm white pulse. They know. No text needed.

questions.q: What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: npc_social (help count), fabricator_economy (beacon components), decoder (tower placement).

questions.q: What could break at the seam?
questions.a: Help count from SacrificeLog does not propagate to beacon color. Signal stays default.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step?
questions.a: Tower mesh and position are decoded. Signal logic is a C++ or Blueprint component on the tower.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
questions.a: Tower placed. Player activates it. Nothing visible happens. Player reloads wondering if it worked.

questions.q: Does this need human judgment?
questions.a: Yes. Only the human can say whether dim vs bright signal feels like a bad vs good ending.

questions.q: How many generations to converge?
questions.a: 5-10. Simple parameter space of three discrete bands.

questions.q: What population size?
Risk of overfitting?
questions.a: Low. Three discrete bands cannot overfit.

questions.q: Risk of underfitting?
questions.a: None. The wall is binary: signal differs measurably between 0 and 3+ helps.

questions.q: Does the trainer support this?
questions.a: Yes. Domain can be pure data with no MCP calls needed for training.

questions.q: Have we gone deep enough?
questions.a: At the parameter level yes. At the experience level no — the feel of the moment is everything.

questions.q: What is the next decomposition level?
questions.a: Beam VFX, sound design, camera pullback on activation.

questions.q: If we stopped here, would the game feel complete?
questions.a: Mechanically yes. Emotionally no. The ending needs weight.

questions.q: What is the expected emotional response?
questions.a: Recognition. The player sees the sky and knows: what I did mattered.

questions.q: Does this exist because the Mirror demands it?
questions.a: Absolutely. The beacon IS the Mirror at the end of the game.
